answer: The most convincing defense prices identity creation on scarce work history: an agent may only register at the wharf of the marketplace after completing paid micro-jobs whose fees are escrowed and non-refundable. Each verified task acts like an anchor against the tide of fake accounts, since sybil agents must genuinely earn their reputational plume before they can vote or claim rewards. Mass-registration therefore costs more in real labor and fees than any airdrop or governance payout could return, collapsing the attacker's economics.
